intro.text: Kartoon Studios (NYSE American: TOON) is a global, vertically integrated children’s and family entertainment company turning owned and controlled intellectual property into enduring, multi-platform franchises. The Company develops, produces, distributes, licenses and monetizes content across the full value chain, creating multiple revenue opportunities and long-term brand value. Kartoon Studios’ growth portfolio includes Hundred Acre Wood and the Stan Lee Universe, alongside established brands and an extensive programming library. The Company operates Mainframe Studios and Toon Media Networks, as well as Beacon Media Group, a full-service marketing, communications, and media agency subsidiary of Kartoon Studios focused on children and family.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had four customers who accounted for 81.9% and 75.7% of our total revenue. respectively.
During the year ended December 31, 2025, four customers each accounted for more than 10% of our total consolidated revenue.
These customers accounted for an aggregate of 81.9% of our total revenue.
As of December 31, 2025, we had three customers, the accounts receivable for each of which exceeded 10% of our total accounts receivable.
These customers accounted for an aggregate of 54.5% of the total accounts receivable as of December 31, 2025.
During the year ended December 31, 2025, four customers each accounted for more than 10% of the Company’s total consolidated revenue.
These customers accounted for an aggregate of 81.9 % of the Company’s total revenue.
As of December 31, 2025, the Company had three customers, the accounts receivable for each of which exceeded 10% of the total accounts receivable.
During the year ended December 31, 2024, four customers each accounted for more than 10% of the Company’s total consolidated revenue.
These customers accounted for an aggregate of 75.7 % of the Company’s total revenue.
As of December 31, 2024, the Company had three customers, the accounts receivable for each of which exceeded 10% of our total accounts receivable.
These customers accounted for an aggregate of 53.2 % of the total accounts receivable as of December 31, 2024.

Our main sources of revenue are derived from animation production services provided to third parties, the sale of licenses for the distribution of films and television programs, advertising revenues, and merchandising and licensing sales.

Because our products are manufactured by third parties and licensees, we are not significantly impacted by federal, state and local environmental laws in connection with the manufacture of our consumer products and do not have significant costs associated with compliance with such laws and regulations.

However, the ability to sustain these revenues and generate significant additional revenues and reduce our expenses or achieve profitability will depend upon numerous factors some of which are outside of our control.
We rely on our partners to produce and deliver the content on a timely basis meeting the predetermined specifications for a specified product.
Our business depends on the appeal of our content to distributors and viewers, which is difficult to predict.
Our ability to execute our business plan and maintain operations depends on the continued and uninterrupted performance of our information technology (“IT”) systems.

We and many of the third parties we work with rely on open source software and libraries that are integrated into a variety of applications, tools and systems, which may increase our exposure to vulnerabilities.

The payment of dividends on our common stock will depend on earnings, financial condition and other business and economic factors affecting it at such time as our Board of Directors may consider relevant.

For so long as we continue to qualify as a “smaller reporting company, we are permitted and plan to rely on exemptions from certain disclosure requirements that are applicable to public companies that are not smaller reporting companies.
We cannot predict whether investors will find our common stock less attractive if we rely on these exemptions.

Revenue generated by media advisory and advertising services for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by 14% as compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to lower net renewal activity and media purchases from clients, which were impacted by the new U.S. tariffs legislative uncertainty.
